subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a new saturated-session compaction guard surface beyond the existing summary-quality checks and post-compaction identical-tool abort, and what config/default/reset policy should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config/default behavior and decides when OpenClaw should strengthen compaction, validate summaries, and recommend reset after degraded session state; source inspection cannot choose that product policy safely.

options.title: Keep As Design Work
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the config namespace, default behavior, validator contract, and reset-recommendation policy before accepting or replacing the config-scaffold PR.

options.title: Fold Into Existing Guard Surfaces
options.body: Constrain follow-up work to the existing `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` and compaction-safeguard quality paths instead of creating `agents.defaults.compaction.guard`.

options.title: Reject New Guard Surface
options.body: Decline the new saturated-session guard direction and rely on current summary quality, the post-compaction identical-tool abort, and narrower compaction-rate-limit work.

recommendation.title: Keep As Design Work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the config namespace, default behavior, validator contract, and reset-recommendation policy before accepting or replacing the config-scaffold PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner signal for current compaction runtime policy because he authored the current squashed files and merged the adjacent post-compaction guard PR.
